sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Real-Time Voice Cloning is an implementation of the SV2TTS research paper. It captures a voice from a few seconds of audio and then generates speech in that voice from any text, with a vocoder fast enough for real time. It comes with a graphical toolbox and a command-line demo.
sixtySeconds.problem: It shows how voice cloning works end to end: a speaker encoder, a Tacotron synthesizer and a WaveRNN vocoder. The author notes it has aged, and that newer projects such as Chatterbox give better quality.
whoFor: Students learning how voice cloning works
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to learn and experiment with a classic voice cloning pipeline. For the best quality today, the README itself recommends newer projects.

overview: This repository was the author's master's thesis. SV2TTS works in three stages: an encoder turns a few seconds of audio into a digital representation of a voice, a synthesizer uses it to generate a spectrogram from text, and a vocoder turns that into audio.

It implements SV2TTS and the GE2E speaker encoder itself, and uses Tacotron and WaveRNN implementations from fatchord/WaveRNN. Pretrained models download automatically, and uv creates the Python environment for you.

The README's own heads-up says the repo has quickly gotten old, that many paid services give better quality, and points to Chatterbox for an open-source project up to date with the 2025 state of the art.
